description: Pale green plates, cool and slightly damp. Some creature grows these; the valley has not shown it.
lore: Every stone in the country comes out of the grass warm and stays warm. Handlers grade by heft in the dark and the warmth is how the hand knows it has hold of a stone and not a pebble. This one is cool. Cool and faintly damp, pale green plates with a brighter seam at every crack, and it does not dry out — a dry shelf in a dry room through a dry month, and you pick it up and it is exactly as you left it. Forty gold. It turns up in junk lots between the teeth and the buckles.

It is the stone people start with, and it is honestly good at what it is for: a whole season of moss and wet clay and slick root, and not once do you go down for footing. Press the graders and they will commit to one sentence, said flatly, on the way to something else — whatever reached the bottom of this spent its life keeping its feet in wet ground. That narrows the valley by about half. It narrows the list of things anyone has ever broken not at all, because this is not on that list. New hands ask. Old hands used to. Somewhere between the two the question aged out, the way questions do here when [[lore/the_hard_pieces|the work]] is steady and the answer costs money, and the stones go on arriving.
gm_notes: Unbound stone number two, deliberately the opposite handling to the opal: cheap, common, everywhere, and nobody is investigating because there is no money in it. The anomaly is domestic — every other soulstone is warm and this one is cool and damp — which is stranger for being boring. The half-a-valley line is the only inference on offer and it is not evidence of anything. Leave the source open.
